DECISIONS:
Q1: A
Q2: A

RATIONALE:
Q1: The fix cannot be made inside the verified heal scope. The touched-set computation that rejects the run is in `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:4440-4467`: a path counts as touched only when it is absent (line 4447) or its blob or exec bit changed (line 4464). Invariant 4 is in `scripts/check_resolver_diff.sh:222-238`, and the missing modify/delete guidance belongs in `prompts/conflict-resolver.txt`, which has no modify/delete text today. None of these paths is in the intake-written `ai:workflow-heal-scope:v1` marker. The pipeline cannot widen that scope: `scripts/implement_heal_preflight.sh` refuses an edited heal body, and `run_heal_plan_scope_gate` in `scripts/files_touched_scope_guard.py` (lines 1260-1289) holds any plan path outside the verified scope. Option B adds almost nothing, because `tests/test_conflict_folded_fragment_keep.py::test_check_resolver_diff_names_an_untouched_unmerged_path` (line 187) already locks in the rejection it would reproduce, and the follow-up issue it relies on is something the pipeline cannot file. Option C leaves a defect in place that recurs on every PR whose base deletes a file the head edits. So the planner writes the full fix as an exact file list, and the heal plan gate is expected to hold it (`heal_scope_plan_paths_missing`) until a maintainer re-scopes or re-files it. The plan must not include steps that edit the issue body, re-file the issue, or act on PR #9452.
Q2: Both parts are needed. Changing only the prompt fixes PR #9452, which needs a `git rm` to honour the base's deliberate deletion recorded in `changelog.d/run-volume-2026-11-sync-throttle-sweep.md`. But keeping a legitimate surviving side would still be rejected, so a person would still have to merge by hand. Changing only the harness adds a `KEEP_SURVIVING_SIDE:` line the model is never told about, and leaves the "do not modify files without conflict markers" rule steering it towards the outcome that is rejected. With both parts, `check_resolver_diff.sh` invariant 4 (lines 222-238) stays strict, so an undeclared, unchanged modify/delete path still fails.

Notes for the planner (binding constraints that follow from these decisions):
- Files to list exactly:
  - `prompts/conflict-resolver.txt` (there is no `prompts/_templates/` twin; checked)
  - `prompts/contracts/conflict-resolver.yml`
  - `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`
  - `scripts/check_resolver_diff.sh`, error text only, which may mention the keep line; the check itself must not be loosened
  - one regression test under `tests/`
  - a `changelog.d/` fragment named after this issue
- Keep-line acceptance applies only when all of these hold:
  - the path has index stages `1 2` or `1 3`;
  - the path is listed in `CONFLICTED_PATHS_FILE`;
  - the file is present and its content is unchanged from the pre-resolver snapshot;
  - it is named on an exact `KEEP_SURVIVING_SIDE: <path>` line in the resolver summary.
- Accepted paths go into `RESOLVER_TOUCHED_FILE`. Staging then goes through the existing `stage_resolver_touched_path_or_fail`.
- Follow the stage-aware keep handling already in the harness (the `CONFLICT_FORWARD_MERGE_FRAGMENT_KEEP_ENABLED` / `CONFLICT_FOLDED_FRAGMENT_KEEP_ENABLED` paths covered by `tests/test_conflict_folded_fragment_keep.py`) rather than adding a competing mechanism. Gate the new behaviour behind a kill switch that defaults to `true` in the script itself (§8).
- The regression fixture is a base that deletes a file the head modified, with three cases:
  - the file is left unchanged with no keep line: it fails with the existing invariant-4 error;
  - the file is deleted: it passes and the deletion is staged;
  - the file is left unchanged with `KEEP_SURVIVING_SIDE:`: it passes and HEAD's copy is staged.
